A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Caption Restoration work despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V3 reports original model evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, human evaluations, and transfer experiments in Table 2, Figure 5, Table 3, and Appendix D.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds VCR-HIDDEN evaluations in Tables 1, 6, and 7 and real-world case-study outcomes in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The VCR formulation, VCR-WIKI masking procedure, and LoRA fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. VCR-HIDDEN varies evaluation inputs and their construction settings, without introducing a new restoration algorithm, model architecture, objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: V4 adds VCR-HIDDEN with non-Wikipedia image-caption pairs and varied caption placement, fonts, resolution, and occlusion conditions. Appendix G additionally evaluates eleven real-world photographs containing occluded or distorted text. These extend the represented input environments beyond the retained synthetic VCR-WIKI evaluations; English and Chinese coverage remains.

E2.justification: The corresponding VCR-WIKI comparisons add DeepSeek-VL2, Ovis2, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL-V2 76B, and Qwen2-VL 72B, while removing DeepSeek-VL 1.3B and Yi-VL 6B result rows. The hidden-test comparisons substantially expand the evaluated roster further, including Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Gemini 2.0, o1, InternVL2.5, and additional model families.

E3.justification: V4 introduces a hidden-test protocol with 100 instances per language, randomized caption position and fonts, mixed easy/hard masking, and widths sampled uniformly between 600 and 1000 pixels. Appendix G adds complete-recovery judgments on eleven photographs before and after fine-tuning. Existing VCR-WIKI splits, metrics, fine-tuning budgets, and human-study procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The hidden evaluation adds testing under changed data sources and rendering conditions, including comparisons with and without visual-image context. Appendix G newly examines whether synthetic-data fine-tuning transfers to real-world text recovery. Existing benchmark-correlation and cross-language transfer analyses are retained. Mismatched ground-truth captions in Figures 16 and 17 limit confidence in those particular new cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrapped standard deviations for benchmark scores and means and standard deviations for human evaluations. The added benchmark tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no new seed counts, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: Matching VCR-WIKI result rows retain their scores, but added and removed models substantially change the reported results and rankings. For example, Table 2 adds Qwen2.5-VL 72B at 31.53% Chinese-hard exact match with image context, alongside the retained Qwen2-VL 7B score of 18.33%. Hidden-test scores and photographic case outcomes are new results under different conditions, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The VCR input formulation and exact-match/Jaccard definitions retain their mathematical meaning. Neither version contains substantive theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution C3 add VCR-HIDDEN as protection against potential overfitting. The central contributions remain the VCR task, synthetic-data pipeline, VCR-WIKI dataset, and evidence of model limitations. The longer title emphasizes pixel-level reasoning already discussed in v3, while the conclusion is essentially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds a rationale for choosing five-gram masking, without a new span-length ablation. Section 4.4 newly attributes poor performance to reasoning or alignment limitations rather than unfamiliar text. It also qualifies the CogVLM2 design explanation as a hypothesis requiring further empirical validation, softening v3's architectural interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix B expands model identifiers and weight links and discloses use of official or OpenRouter APIs. V4 documents hidden-test construction and its non-public status. Conversely, it drops the explicit CC BY-SA 4.0 statement and direct augmentation-script pointer from v3. Core fine-tuning hyperparameters and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting the expanded model inventory, including Qwen2.5-VL, DeepSeek-VL2, Molmo, InternVL2.5, and o1. The related-work discussion and positioning against VQA and OCR remain substantially unchanged; this is a model-literature update rather than a major repositioning.

P1.justification: V4 changes the title, edits the abstract and introduction, and substantially condenses portions of Section 2. Model descriptions move into Appendix B, and existing appendices are reordered around the additions. The main section sequence and much of the experimental discussion, related work, conclusion, and retained appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V4 adds three hidden-test tables and eleven photographic figures with correctness annotations. It expands and reformats comparison tables, adds italic highlighting for pre-release models, groups model specifications by family, and relocates dataset statistics into Appendix A with a hidden-test column. Existing Figures 1-6 retain their content. Figures 16-17 introduce visibly mismatched ground-truth captions.

improvement.justification: V4 broadens the benchmark's empirical support through non-Wikipedia hidden evaluation and newer model comparisons, and more carefully qualifies the CogVLM2 mechanism explanation. These gains are limited by unspecified hidden-data sources and simultaneous changes in input conditions, which prevent isolating overfitting effects. The mismatched ground-truth captions in Figures 16-17 also weaken the new real-world evidence. Overall, the expanded evaluation offers a limited net improvement while the established results and central conclusions remain largely unchanged.
